recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If terminal-period normalization regresses in generated outputs, follow up in the FHIR Publisher/build tooling rather than patching individual source cells in this repository.
issue_request: FHIR-18493 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core narrative issue raised against STU3 and applied for R5. It asked for consistency about periods at the end of definitions, with a resolution to add logic that appends periods to definitions, usage notes, profiles, value sets, code systems, and similar infrastructure text if feasible.
initial_application: No searched source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-18493. Adjacent Narrative issues FHIR-18492 and FHIR-18494 were applied directly to source/datatypes/narrative.xml, but the FHIR-I minutes for FHIR-18493 recorded it as a tooling issue and agreed to fix tooling, which matches the absence of a direct source-text patch.
additional_context: Narrative remains active and normative in the current build according to source/fhir.ini. The spreadsheet source still contains some Narrative and NarrativeStatus input cells without terminal periods, while current CI and R5 generated outputs for narrative.profile.json/xml, codesystem-narrative-status, and valueset-narrative-status include periods. The FHIR source checkout does not contain the publisher Java tooling that performs this normalization.
reconciliation: Made no source change and published an empty audit commit. The current built specification already presents the affected generated/profile and terminology definitions with terminal periods, so editing isolated spreadsheet cells would duplicate the tooling policy rather than implement the Jira resolution.

related_jiras.note: Adjacent Narrative definition issue applied directly to the same spreadsheet by commit 9cad63bc63, showing direct source wording changes were tracked separately.
Adjacent NarrativeStatus definition issue applied directly to the same code-list rows by commit 7550ccbfa7, while FHIR-18493 remained a tooling-level punctuation decision.
Separate terminal-period correction already represented on the combined branch; it illustrates related punctuation auditing but was not redecided here.
